item.title: What Would an Interim U.S.-Mexico Trade Deal Actually Involve?
item.description: Mexico is close to an interim deal with the United States. What it concedes for tariff relief today could set the baseline for North America down the line.

item.title: The Levantine Opportunity in a Churning Middle East
item.description: The wars of the past three years have eroded the fragile order of the Middle East. Now, for the first time in decades, the Levant has a chance to create a new alignment and build a regional order centered around strong, inclusive states, stability, and open trade.

item.title: Amid Iran War Tensions, Energy Market Resilience Wears Thin
item.description: Fresh attacks on energy infrastructure in the Middle East may push regional leaders to build the first post-U.S. security arrangement for the Strait of Hormuz. As U.S. voters head to the polls in a few weeks, an expensive war linked to affordability concerns will be top of mind.

item.title: The U.S.-China Summit: Too Big and Too Small to Fail
item.description: Scott Kennedy argues that although the Trump-Xi summit will likely extend the current period of stability, the gap between the convening’s limited ambitions and the growing challenges facing the world points to a growing vacuum of global leadership.

item.title: Paraguay’s Next Development Chapter
item.description: Paraguay today has the potential to transform its development story, but it will require close cooperation with international partners to make the best use of its advantages.

item.title: Is the U.S. Banking System Ready for a Post-Quantum Future?
item.description: Sultan Meghji argues that the hardest cryptographic deadline facing U.S. banks is being set by SWIFT and foreign supervisors, not Washington. Adversaries are harvesting encrypted financial traffic now. Three of the four fixes require no new statutory authority.

item.title: The AI Industry Is Coalescing on “Pacing the Frontier.” Will It Actually Change Anything?
item.description: Over the past week, frontier labs, policymakers, and the U.S. public have reached remarkable consensus around calls to pace AI development. What now? Aalok Mehta outlines the four steps government and industry must take to translate the current moment into durable change.
